details:
As someone currently learning Udon I was surprised to find out objects can't actually be parented to players, instead you need to follow the player's position and rotation. This method works, but isn't as efficient, especially at scale. Being able to parent to a player, or have something to parent to, would be more straightforward. 

I started wondering if the reason why not was due to concerns over parenting causing issues with avatars, and then realized an ideal-solution: PlayerObjects. If PlayerObjects were automatically attached to the player themselves (or could be with an optional checkbox), the parenting could be specially set up by VRchat devs in a way that doesn't cause issues, and creators could simply attach objects to the parented playerobject. It should also theoretically keep existing follow-based systems functional and even work alongside them if needed (e.g. a game prefab).

Alternatively, a separate component, a PlayerParent or ParentPoint, that allows parenting onto avatars and can be added/removed as needed. Ideally one per player. This would be ideal for if a set of code expects/needs all playerobjects to be in one place.

Essentially, having a point on an avatar that creators can successfully mount an object to, rather than having objects follow players.
title: Parent playerobjects to players (so objects can be parented to players)
